unit.name: DQN training stabilization: terminal states and replay memory
unit.description: Introduces implementation issues that arise when training DQNs and the methods used to handle terminal steps and correlated experience.
unit.summary: The training section revisits DQN implementation and highlights that terminal states must be handled specially because there is no next-state future reward after the episode ends [ts=3670s] [ts=3714s]. The instructor modifies the loop by creating a terminal-state boolean and checking whether s' is terminal before computing the target [ts=3846s] [ts=3872s]. Experience replay stores transitions of the form phi(s), action, reward, and phi(s') in a memory buffer rather than training only on the most recent transition [ts=3915s] [ts=3972s]. Sampling mini-batches from replay memory exposes the model to older useful experiences, supports mini-batch gradient descent, and reduces the problem of consecutive samples being highly correlated [ts=4032s] [ts=4170s].

key_points.text: Terminal states require special handling because the target should not include discounted future reward after the episode has ended.
A DQN implementation can maintain a terminal boolean and check whether s' is terminal before computing the Bellman target.
Experience replay stores transitions such as phi(s), action, reward, and phi(s') in replay memory D.
Replay memory allows random mini-batch sampling from past experiences rather than updating only from the newest transition.
One advantage of experience replay is breaking strong correlation between consecutive experiences in a game trajectory.

kp_catalog.name: Terminal-state handling in DQN
kp_catalog.description: Detecting terminal states so target computation does not include future Q-values after an episode ends.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor explicitly adds a terminal boolean to the DQN loop and says terminal transitions cannot be handled the same way as non-terminal ones [ts=3714s] [ts=3846s].

kp_catalog.name: Experience replay
kp_catalog.description: A memory buffer of past transitions sampled randomly for mini-batch updates to improve data reuse and reduce correlation.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Experience replay is presented as a training challenge solution and incorporated into the DQN algorithm [ts=3915s] [ts=4032s].

kp_catalog.name: DQN target, loss, and gradient update
kp_catalog.description: Bootstrapped training of a Q-network using y = r + gamma max Q(s',a') as a target and regression loss against Q(s,a).
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The DQN target, loss, and update rule are the main technical bridge from tabular RL to deep RL.
